title: The factory, heard through its machinery
intro: A working library of cropped recordings for Loopforge. Each sound should make an action or a change in the factory tangible: contact, load, resistance, release. Keep ordinary interaction quiet enough that a jam or a consequential decision can take the foreground.
reviewNote: Play each edit to review it. These are the prepared source levels; the game mixes them more quietly. Only one preview plays at a time. Leaving this tab or hiding the page pauses playback. Crop timing, fades and decoded peaks have been checked; final timbre and mix approval needs a listening pass in the game.
licenseNote: Five owner-selected Freesound recordings, all marked CC0 when checked on 8 October 2026. The six edits retain their source credits, exact crop intervals and processing recipe. The original downloads remain untouched. No Freesound audio is fetched at runtime.

clips.name: Menu · metal meets concrete
clips.role: Confirm a main-menu destination with a physical clang. No hover sound. Its decay continues through the page transition.
clips.edit: Removed the leading silence; retained both contacts and the falling metallic resonance. Short attack fade and an 80 ms tail fade. No arbitrary playback offset.
clips.review: Does this carry the same weight as the landing artwork without becoming tiring on repeat visits?

clips.name: RESET · motor contactor
clips.role: The red RESET button energizes the drive. The same contactor marks first-shift startup. A distinct mechanism from the menu clang.
clips.edit: Removed just over one second of idle recording. Kept the small movement before contact, the sharp main hit and its short decay; 45 ms tail fade.
clips.review: The button should engage immediately. A sustained motor rising under it is still a separate sound to source.

clips.name: Commitment · ratchet locks
clips.role: A compact mechanical confirmation for approving a plan, resolving a decision and committing the output allocation in the first shift.
clips.edit: Isolated the complete engagement stroke, including its individual teeth. Removed the long wait before the later release; 25 ms tail fade.
clips.review: It should feel like a choice engaging a mechanism. Follow, override and irreversible allocation still need more distinct treatments.

clips.name: Shutdown · latch releases
clips.role: Release the working shift into the output-allocation stage. A small opening click followed by the mechanism settling.
clips.edit: Kept the release click, the physical interval and the settling thud as one action. Removed the surrounding dead time; 45 ms tail fade.
clips.review: Does this read as machinery disengaging, rather than another reward or approval?

clips.name: Heavy gate · hinge and latch
clips.role: Candidate for a security gate, a heavy room closure or a substantial mechanical transition. No gameplay assignment yet.
clips.edit: The source was already trimmed. Kept the full hinge-and-latch gesture instead of cutting it into an unexplained impact. Added 4 ms / 100 ms boundary fades.
clips.review: Find a visible moving mechanism that justifies the whole gesture; avoid playing three seconds of gate motion for a small UI click.

clips.name: Dark room · feedback atmosphere
clips.role: A candidate environmental texture from the long synthetic soundscape. This is neither the conveyor drive nor the future soundtrack.
clips.edit: Selected 01:00–01:26 of the 20-minute recording. A two-second overlap produces a 24-second loop; held at a lower level with stereo retained.
clips.review: Listen across the loop boundary. Judge whether its unease fits a particular room and whether it leaves space for mechanisms and speech.

direction: Synchronize the strike with the visible contact. Mechanical settling can continue after an order is accepted; sound must never delay the command or invent a game outcome.
Let routine production sit underneath decisions and accidents. Coalesce repeated cues at faster playback; leave room for the factory to fall quiet.
Load, strain, jam and restart should sound related. Their timing comes from resolved world events and presentation state, independently of model calls.
Later stems can carry working rhythm, mounting pressure, deliberation and aftermath. Do not turn every produced robot into a musical victory.

No automatic preview playback. Gameplay sound is user-enabled, hidden-page work stops, and readable visual feedback carries every important state. Review-only recordings are never loaded by the playable shift.
gaps: Procedural low motor bed exists. Still need chain/roller motion, load variations, coast-down and restart rise.
Visual jam/alarm exists on the landing. Recorded strain, jam impact and a restrained repeating alarm are still missing there.
A procedural connection cue exists. Distinct supervisor signatures, relay opening/closing and transmission texture are still to develop.
Both currently share the commitment ratchet. Develop a legible difference in transmission and response without making override sound automatically wrong.
Procedural batch cue exists. Outtake clatter, quota dispatch and retained-worker activation need distinct sounds and synchronization.
Procedural warning and impact exist. A coordinated impact, machine cutoff, quiet gap and restart remain to be directed.
Gate and dark-room crops are audition candidates. No dedicated per-room ambience is implemented.
Not sourced or implemented. Plan separate music control, stems and ducking under important signals.
